thread.title: Samsung falls on Weaker than Expected Guidance

author: Bryan Shin
title: Samsung falls on Weaker than Expected Guidance
text:
01/08/2019 437
Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. provided its fourth-quarter guidance on Tuesday and forecasted declining profits. Samsung shares dipped by 1.68% on the Korean Stock Exchange following the results.
For the fourth quarter, Samsung said it predicts operating profit in the range of KRW 10.7 Trillion to KRW 10.9 Trillion (USD 9.52 Billion to USD 9.70 Billion), which would represent approximately a 28.7% decline year over year. Analysts are forecasting an operating profit of KRW 13.2 Trillion (USD 11.74 Billion), which is over 18% higher than Samsung’s guidance.
Estimates are already well below Samsung’s third-quarter operating profit results of KRW 17.57 Trillion (USD 15.63 Billion) and below the Company’s operating profit of KRW 14.87 Trillion (USD 13.23 Billion) back in its June quarter last year.
Samsung said that its weaker guidance is likely due to a decrease in demand for its memory chip business as well as growing competition within the smartphone industry. The weaker demand for memory chips is leading to an overall decline in shipments and a drop off in chip prices.
Samsung predicts consolidated sales for the fourth quarter to be approximately KRW 59 Trillion (USD 52.50 Billion), which is also lower than Reuters’ forecast of KRW 62.8 Trillion (55.88 Billion).
The Company expects quarterly sales to come in at approximately KRW 58 Trillion to KRW 60 Trillion (USD 51.61 Billion to USD 53.39 Billion)
“What’s happening is that memory demand has really fallen off a cliff in (the fourth quarter),” Mark Newman, Managing Director at Sanford C. Bernstein, told CNBC’s “Street Signs” on Tuesday. He said that much of the weakness in the predicted numbers is due to “data center demand being pushed down, and also smartphone’s (demand is) pretty weak.”
Samsung’s guidance comes shortly after Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) announced its weaker guidance last week. Apple Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook disclosed in the release that the Company is lowering its forecast primarily due to weaker demand in China amid the ongoing trade war tensions between the U.S.
However, Samsung did not disclose in its guidance that China is impacting its earnings, but that “ mounting ” macroeconomic uncertainites are affecting its business.
Despite Samsung not disclosing whether or not China is impacting its business, analysts believe that increasing competition stemming from China is a factor.
“There is obviously the competition from the Chinese players that is limiting the growth of Samsung in many markets including the high-growth ones like India and South East Asia,” said Kiranjeet Kaur, a Singapore-based analyst with research firm IDC, according to CNN .
Samsung is expected to report its fourth quarter financial results at the end of the month. Pin 0 0 shares
